title: The Empty Box
subtitle: A riddle whose answer is determined by its solver.

items.text: The Empty Box

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Jones.
Around the usual time, Bette arrives at Jones's ward—only to find a neatly wrapped gift box tied with a silk ribbon sitting on her chair.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Huh? A present? Who is it from?
She realizes a bit too late she shouldn't have said it so strangely; the gift is light, almost as if nothing were inside.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: No, it's from me to you.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: What for? Did I forget a special occasion?
Bette looks at Jones in surprise, about to open the box to see what is inside.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Don't open it yet.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Hm?
Jones stops her just as her fingers begin to pull on the ribbon and gestures for her to sit down.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: This was the first gift I ever received—from my mother.
Hearing that, Bette examines the box even more curiously, turning it over in her hands.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: What's inside?

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: It's a beautiful box—so beautiful that I thought it could be worth a lot of money on its own. I spent a long time trying to figure out what could be inside.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Cotton, stamps, banknotes ... even fairy dust.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: I kept asking my mother for hints, but she wouldn't tell me.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Why didn't you just open it up and see?

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Because ...
Jones lets out a sigh.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: I was afraid.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: It was my first real Christmas gift. I was terrified that if I opened it, It'd be empty.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Rather than finding out there was nothing inside, I figured it would be better to leave it as it was—so it could always be a "gift."

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: After all, the joy of receiving a present is the most important part, isn't it?

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: If I opened it, and it was empty, what would I do? It'd be the same either way.
A small wavering doubt stirs inside Bette.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Then ... what did you end up doing?

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: I placed it on my bedside table and held back the urge to open it—it sat there for ten years, maybe more.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Then, a director discovered me as I was interviewing to be a waitress and cast me in a film.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Holding the payment from that movie, I finally had the courage to face the mystery of that box.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Before opening it, I bought myself an expensive bracelet. If the box was empty, I'd put the bracelet inside and treat it as the first gift I ever gave myself.
Jones lies in the glass chamber, watching Bette.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: So ... was there something inside?
Jones seems to smile, but the movement of the bandages is so slight that Bette wonders if she is only imagining it.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: It doesn't matter what is in there. I had already realized by then that I couldn't live my life waiting for dreams. Whether I became a star or not.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Ah ...

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Before I said anything, how would you have imagined my childhood?
Bette looks at Jones's bandaged face, trying to imagine what she would have looked like as a child.
But no matter how hard she tries, her mind can only picture something on a black-and-white screen—on it, Jones is sometimes a wealthy heiress, sometimes a poor country girl.
But the real Jones isn't someone on a silver screen. She is flesh and blood, born into this world just like everyone else.
Bette resists her initial thought.
To imagine her as just another girl—even if she knows it's true—feels wrong; it feels like taking something away from her.
It would mean she wasn't born to be the star that she became, that she didn't have any special gift to light up the screen, and that she's no different from her.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Why? Why are you giving this to me? Is there something inside?
Jones shakes her head once more.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Hm?
Behind the door, Laura enters, pushing a medical cart.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: Visiting time is over. Miss Jones needs her treatment, and I'm going to need you to leave.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Go on, Bette. I'll see you later.
Bette looks down at the box with newfound anxiety.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: It is exquisitely wrapped, with a delicate ribbon tied into a bow on top. The knot is neat and smooth, as if no force had been applied to it in the tying.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: Time to go.
Laura pushes Bette's shoulder gently, ushering her out of the ward.
Bette examines the box from every angle as she walks toward her room. Her feet shuffling and slow.
She shakes it as she holds her ear against it, but even that reveals nothing.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: What does it mean? Is it just an empty box, like false hope?
Whispering tendrils seem to seep in from the corridor's shadows, filling her with a quiet sensation of fear.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Maybe Jones figured it out? Could she have seen through the illusion I created for her?

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: But ...
Bette searches her memory of their last conversation; she had been different, but not in a way that revealed anything.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: So, why give me this box?

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Should I do the same thing—wait until I have something to give myself before opening it?
People hurry past her, but Bette hasn't moved in what feels like minutes.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: I must be different from her. Because even if this box is empty, I don't think I'd feel disappointed ...

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Because ...
The thought crosses her mind and is met with a sudden panic that crawls up her spine.
She yanks off the ribbon.
It isn't empty. A reel of film is bound in the middle to prevent it from making any sound when shaken.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: What ...
The cutting and splicing technique is immediately familiar. This is her film.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: How ...
Bette removes the film.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Jones has been in that glass chamber this entire time. So who helped her retrieve the film? Who wrapped it up like this?
A suspicion races up to the front of her mind, one that drives her to turn and then run back toward the ward.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Jones!
Laura is injecting some kind of medication into Jones through the glass chamber's tubes.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: Oh dear.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: You opened it.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: I did. So, you knew? The "Storm" ...

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Yeah.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Did she tell you?

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: Don't glare at me like that. She asked first.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: But ... it doesn't really matter. The world outside looks just as beautiful as the pictures, and it's safe ...
Bette steps toward Jones's chamber.

items.speaker: Laura
items.text: I got what I was here for. I'm leaving.
Pushing the syringe empty, Laura packs up her things, grabs the motionless camera from the table by the door, and leaves the room without another word.
Bette isn't quite sure yet what to make of this scene. But she hasn't given up.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: The camera doesn't matter. I can buy another one. I've already rewritten the script.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Once you get better, even without the director and crew, we can still finish things.
Bette approaches Jones, looking up at her in the chamber, which now seems more like a glass coffin, as if pleading for a princess to awaken.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: You will finish it. I'm sure of that.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: This movie is yours now. I want you to complete it; that's why I wanted you to have the film.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: But what about you ...

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: My days on the silver screen are over, Bette. Just look at me; I'm not star material anymore.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: I'm going to be stuck here in this thing for ... the rest of my life.
Jones says it all as if it were just lines in a script—a first read-through. No emotions needed.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: No. That's not true!
Bette's voice trembles.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: They said your recovery is going well. That you'll be able to get out of this bed soon.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: And didn't you see your face that night? We ... that night ...

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: I have a mole; I always had it covered up on set. But you would have seen it ... if it were still there. The rest was perfect—right down to the eyebrows.
She had tried so hard to recreate her face. But Jones is right; she never saw the mole. Her scars had covered up all of it.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: So ... you already knew ...

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Do you remember me saying that you remind me of someone?
Jones's eyes have begun to flutter, looking more and more heavy.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: You remind me of ... well, me.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Always waiting for someone else to give you what you need. Not realizing that you ... had the power to get it for yourself.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: I saw your dream as you see it, on that silver rectangle, and it's going to be beautiful. But I won't be your star.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: You look wonderful on camera, and you look best when you're wearing your own face.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: Now it's your role. Your movie ... Finish it ...
Her voice fades out, as if being pulled into a heavy slumber.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Jones? What's going on? What's happening to you?
Bette turns in horror to realize the liquid that the nurse injected has already drained completely into Jones's body.
She pounds on the glass, trying to grab Jones's attention. But her friend is slipping away from her, like an anchor falling into unseen depths.

items.speaker: Bette
items.text: Jones!

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: I asked for this ... Bette.
The voice is a clear and crisp whisper.

items.speaker: Jones
items.text: A sweet and eternal dream.
我真讨厌这里。
I hate this place.
You haven't got my eyebrows right at all!
Now it's your role. Your movie ... Finish it ...
A sweet and eternal dream.
THE END
